subject: Cloud Computing
title: Infrastructure as Code
description: A micro-lesson that makes Infrastructure as Code usable.

hook.text: An engineer clicks through the AWS console and creates 50 resources. Can anyone recreate this setup? No.

buildup.text: Infrastructure as Code defines your entire cloud setup in text files. Servers, networks, and permissions — all in code.

discovery.text: Tools like Terraform and CloudFormation let you version, review, and reproduce infrastructure like software.

twist.text: IaC eliminates 'it works on my account' problems. Every environment is identical because they come from the same code.

climax.text: Disaster recovery becomes trivial: delete everything and re-run the code. Your entire cloud rebuilds from scratch.

punchline.text: Click-ops breaks at scale. Code your infrastructure instead.

quiz.question: What is the main benefit of Infrastructure as Code?
options: Reproducible, version-controlled infrastructure that can be rebuilt from scratch
It makes cloud resources run faster than manually created ones
It eliminates the need for cloud provider accounts

details.summary: Infrastructure as code defines cloud resources in declarative configuration files that are version-controlled and reproducible. Tools like Terraform, Pulumi, and CloudFormation replace manual console clicks with automated, repeatable infrastructure provisioning.
details.whyItMatters: Manual infrastructure setup is error-prone and impossible to audit. IaC ensures environments are consistent, changes are tracked in version control, and entire stacks can be recreated from scratch.
takeaways: Infrastructure is defined in version-controlled config files
Environments are consistent and reproducible across stages
Changes are reviewed in pull requests like application code

faq.question: What is the difference between Terraform and CloudFormation?
faq.answer: Terraform is provider-agnostic and works across AWS, Azure, GCP, and others using HCL syntax. CloudFormation is AWS-only and uses JSON or YAML. Terraform offers more flexibility for multi-cloud, while CloudFormation integrates more deeply with AWS services.

faq.question: What is drift detection in infrastructure as code?
faq.answer: Drift occurs when actual infrastructure diverges from the defined code, often due to manual changes. Drift detection tools compare live state against the code and flag discrepancies. Regular drift checks ensure the code remains the single source of truth.
